# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b19 - Mandatory domain migration bridge

**Existing beta users must install b19 and restart Home Assistant before installing the later release that changes the actual integration domain to `environment_manager`.**

Beta19 intentionally still uses the legacy Home Assistant domain `air_quality_advisor`. This is required because HACS manages one integration directory per repository: an existing installation must first receive code in its current local directory that knows how to hand the config entry over when the new package appears.

## What b19 changes

Under b19 alone, runtime behavior is the same as beta18. Room Environment limits, room-selected sensor feedback, per-device quiet/occupancy controls, Task AI, Home grouping and safety/ownership protections continue unchanged.

The new code is a dormant migration bridge. On a later restart, if Home Assistant can load a custom integration named `environment_manager`, the bridge does not load any old-domain entity platforms. Instead it schedules a one-time in-place migration after the old config-entry setup lock is released.

## Identity-preserving handoff

The migration is designed to preserve:
- the exact Home Assistant config-entry ID;
- every configuration subentry ID, including Home and room groups;
- entity IDs and entity-registry IDs;
- entity unique IDs, custom names/icons/areas and disabled/hidden state;
- device-registry IDs, custom names/areas and disabled state;
- saved integration data/options.

Before writing anything, the bridge checks for new-domain entity unique-ID or device-identifier conflicts. Entity registry entries are moved from platform `air_quality_advisor` to `environment_manager`. Only Manager-owned device identifier namespaces are rewritten from the old domain to the new domain.

The old config entry is then removed using Home Assistant's low-level no-cleanup replacement path and a new-domain ConfigEntry is inserted with the **same entry ID**. Entity/device registry cleanup is deliberately not run because the entry identity is being retained.

## Why two releases are necessary

A single HACS release cannot safely install both the old migration shim and the new integration directory because HACS manages one integration directory per repository. Beta19 installs the bridge in the old path first. The following domain-switch release can then install the new package while the b19 local bridge remains available for the one-time restart migration.

Do not skip directly from b18 or earlier to the final domain-switch beta. If you do, the old local integration may not contain the migration bridge.

## Validation

Publication is gated by the full Python 3.13/3.14 regression suite, deterministic translations/controller help, frontend tests, Hassfest and HACS. An additional isolated Home Assistant 2026.10 registry test verifies the bridge's platform/identifier migration while preserving entry/subentry/entity/device IDs and user customizations.

No live user installation or physical equipment is operated by these tests. Stable **v0.5.1** remains Latest.
